In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new DNA-based aptasensors for the detection of small molecules and proteins, using hemin/G-quartet structures that function as DNAzymes.
the design of DNA-based aptasensors for the detection of proteins and small molecules using the hemin/G-quadruplex DNAzyme structures.
the design and development of novel chemiluminescent and CRET aptasensors based on the use of DNAzymes formed by the incorporation of hemin in the thrombin and ATP aptamer/G-quadrupex structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hemin/G4 aptasensor systems are highly sensitive, selective, and versatile for the detection of target molecules.

the use of hemin/G-quartet structures in aptasensing assays is very attractive because it enables the use of simple and inexpensive luminol/H( 2)O( 2) chemiluminescent reactions, which can also be used for the development of CRET assays.

the hemin/G-quadraplexes are a versatile platform for the development of aptamer sensors for the detection of proteins, nucleoside triphosphates and other small molecules, by chemiluminescent or CRET processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of hemin/G-quartet complexes into G-quadruplex assemblies yields active DNAzyme nanostructures that can catalyze the oxidation of luminol/H2O2 to generate chemiluminescent signals.
we developed a novel CRET aptasensor platform for the detection of small molecules, based on a hemin/G-quartet catalytic DNAzyme.
we have developed new aptasensors for the detection of ATP and thrombin using chemiluminescent or luminescent DNAzymes and CRET processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of hemin/G-quartet structures as DNAzymes for the catalytic generation of chemiluminiscence or the CRET powering of QDs can lead to sensitive aptasensors for the detection of proteins or other biomolecules.
the hemin/Gquadruplex DNA nanostructures, which are formed in the presence of thrombin or in the presence of ATP, are excellent catalysts for the generation of chemluminescence or CRET processes.

the hemin/G- quadruplex nanostructures can be used for the detection of a wide variety of analytes, by using either the DNAzyme catalyzed chemiluminescent process or the CRET process, which are both triggered by the formation of a G-quadruplex/hemin/thrombin complex.
